mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during tightening periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over three months signals a strengthening demand in the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of increasing real estate sales.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, which leads to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of declining industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong labor market improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, indicates a robust consumer demand and a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong consumer demand and labor market improvement.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month signals inflationary pressure, which leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained growth in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strong economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of GDP growth.
